sections.heading: 重要事实
sections.text:
• 2022年，由于自付医疗支出占家庭预算的10%或更多，全球超过16亿人面临陷入贫困或更深度贫困的风险。

• 到2030年，在低收入和中等收入国家扩大初级卫生保健干预措施可以挽救6000万人的生命，并将平均预期寿命提高3.7岁。

• 据估计，可持续发展目标预计的健康收益中有75%可以通过初级卫生保健实现。

• 为实现初级卫生保健目标，需要每年追加约2000亿至3280亿美元投资，用于更全面的一揽子卫生保健服务。

sections.heading: 何为初级卫生保健？
sections.text:
1978年以来，初级卫生保健的概念经一再重新诠释和定义，导致该术语及其实践上的含混不清。现已制定一个简单明了的定义，以促进全球、国家和地方各级今后初级卫生保健工作的协调，并指导其实施：

“初级卫生保健是一种全社会参与卫生事业的方法，旨在确保实现最高可能水平的健康和福祉及其公平分配，为此应在从健康促进和疾病预防到治疗、康复和姑息治疗的连续过程中尽早关注人们的需求，并尽可能贴近人们的日常环境”。世卫组织和儿童基金会。《二十一世纪初级卫生保健愿景：迈向全民健康覆盖和可持续发展目标》。

初级卫生保健包括三个相互关联和协同增效的组成部分，包括：初级保健和公共卫生产品并作为核心部分发挥作用的综合卫生服务；处理上游和更广泛健康问题决定因素的多部门政策和行动；调动个人、家庭和社区的参与并赋予其权能，以提高社会参与度，增强对健康的自我护理和自立能力。

初级卫生保健植根于对社会正义、公平、团结和参与的承诺。它基于这样一种认识，即享受最高而能获致之健康标准，为人人不分轩轾皆应拥有的基本权利之一。

为切实普及全民健康覆盖，需要从围绕疾病和机构设计的卫生系统转向为民众而设计并由民众参与的卫生系统。初级卫生保健要求各级政府强调超越卫生部门采取行动的重要性，以便对卫生采取全政府方针，包括将健康融入所有政策，高度重视公平和跨越生命全程的干预措施。

初级卫生保健处理健康的更广泛决定因素，并侧重于身体、精神以及社会健康和福祉的全面和相互关联的方面。它为生命全程的健康需要提供全人保健，而不仅限于诊治一系列特定疾病。初级卫生保健确保人们在尽可能贴近日常环境的情况下获得优质全面保健，从促进和预防到治疗、康复和姑息治疗。

sections.heading: 初级卫生保健为何重要？
sections.text:
会员国承诺将振兴和实施初级卫生保健作为促进全民健康覆盖的可持续卫生系统、卫生相关可持续发展目标和卫生安全的基石。初级卫生保健为全民健康覆盖、卫生相关可持续发展目标和卫生安全提供“规划引擎”。《阿斯塔纳宣言》、随附的世界卫生大会72/2号决议、《全民健康覆盖全球监测报告》和联合国大会全民健康覆盖问题高级别宣言都写入并重申了这一承诺。全民健康覆盖、卫生相关可持续发展目标和卫生安全目标十分宏伟，但完全可以实现。迫切需要加快进展，初级卫生保健则为此提供手段。

初级卫生保健是提高人民身心健康和社会福祉的最包容、最公平、最合算、最高效的方法。初级卫生保健投资可产生广泛影响，这方面的的证据在世界各地所在多有，特别是在2019冠状病毒病（COVID-19）大流行等危机时期。

全球范围对初级卫生保健的投资改善了卫生服务的公平性和可及性、卫生保健绩效、卫生系统问责和卫生健康结果。其中一些因素与卫生系统和卫生服务的获得直接相关，但证据清楚表明，卫生服务以外广泛存在的因素在增进健康和福祉方面发挥了关键作用。这些因素包括社会保护、粮食体系、教育和环境因素等。

初级卫生保健的至关重要性，还体现在可促使卫生系统面对危机更具抗御力，更能主动发现流行病的早期迹象，同时随时准备尽早采取行动应对服务需求的激增。尽管证据仍在不断变化，但人们普遍认识到，初级卫生保健是卫生系统的“一线”，是加强应对COVID-19等公共卫生危机的基本公共卫生职能的基础。

sections.heading: 世卫组织的应对
sections.text:
世卫组织正在帮助各国将其卫生系统转向初级卫生保健，以此作为实现全民健康覆盖、可持续发展目标3和卫生安全的重要手段。卫生系统应当适合人、适合环境、适合目的。加强卫生系统涉及加强卫生治理和筹资；卫生人力；性别平等、公平和权利；信息系统；质量和患者安全；孕产妇、新生儿、儿童和青少年健康，直至健康老龄化；性和生殖健康；药物和医疗物资；突发事件防范、应对和恢复；开展传染病和非传染性疾病相关工作等等。

世卫组织确定了在世界范围加强初级卫生保健的三个战略工作领域：

• 根据各国国情和重点，为会员国提供支持实施初级卫生保健的“一站式”机制。这包括落实《初级卫生保健业务框架》，利用COVID-19应对措施带来的投资机会，在恢复工作中重建并健全以初级卫生保健为基础的卫生系统。世界各国和各地区的现有工作和经验将驱动这一核心职能，并为此奠定基础。

• 生成面向初级卫生保健的证据和创新，更加关注掉队人员。这项工作将建立在现有实施证据、最佳实践指南和实施方案、成功国家的专门知识以及为促成创新性解决办法而发表的文献基础上。主要可交付成果包括评估国家初级卫生保健进展的监测和衡量指南，之后的全球初级卫生保健进展报告，以及作为世卫组织学院一部分的创新能力建设工作。

• 通过政策领导、宣传和与政府、非政府组织、民间社会组织、发展伙伴、联合国姊妹机构、捐助者以及全球、区域和国家各级其它利益攸关方的战略伙伴关系，促进振兴初级卫生保健。除其它举措外，这一工作流程还将建立一个初级卫生保健问题外部战略咨询小组，就世界范围内初级卫生保健的振兴向世卫组织提供建议；将设立一个初级卫生保健奖，用于表彰全球初级卫生保健领域的杰出表现；将促进新的初级卫生保健伙伴关系和合作网络，吸收新的利益攸关方，如年轻的卫生领导者、议员以及更广泛民间社会。

sections.heading: Key facts
sections.text:
• Essential medicines treat the priority health-care needs of populations.

• Essential medicines should be available, affordable and of assured quality at all times.

• WHO publishes its Model List of Essential Medicines every 2 years to guide countries to develop and update national essential medicine lists.

• WHO selects essential medicines based on public health relevance, evidence of benefits and harms, and with consideration of costs, affordability and other relevant factors.

• Globally, over 150 countries have national essential medicines lists based on the WHO Model List.

• The 2025 edition of the WHO Model List includes over 520 medicines (including 374 for children).

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Essential medicines are those that effectively and safely treat the priority health-care needs of populations. They are selected by taking into consideration public health relevance, evidence of benefits and harms, and with consideration of costs, affordability and other relevant factors.

Essential medicines should always be available within functioning health systems, in sufficient quantities to meet patient needs. They should be available in appropriate dosage forms for the intended uses and patients, be of assured quality, and be affordable for both individuals and the health system.

While essential medicines cover a wide range of global health needs, they represent only a small proportion of the total number of medicines available globally. The use of a limited number of carefully selected medicines can lead to improved supply, better prescribing practices and lower costs.

Every 2 years since 1977, WHO has published the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (also known as the Essential Medicines List or EML).

sections.heading: Impact and implementation
sections.text:
Over 150 countries have adopted national lists of essential medicines based on the WHO Model List. Essential medicines lists serve as a basis for procurement and supply of medicines in the public sector, reimbursement and insurance schemes, medicine donations and local medicine production (1) . When properly implemented, the essential medicines concept can help improve health outcomes and achieve progress towards universal health coverage. The concept has been successfully implemented in various countries and regions. Studies have shown that essential medicines lists are associated with greater availability of essential medicines than non-essential medicines (2) , increased access (3) , better prescribing and quality of care, and cost savings (4) .

The essential medicines concept can be adapted to different health-care systems, settings and income levels. By focusing on a limited number of carefully selected medicines, countries can improve supply, promote more rational prescribing practices and better control costs while ensuring access to essential medicines.

sections.heading: Challenges
sections.text:
Despite progress, challenges remain in ensuring universal access to essential medicines. Availability and affordability of essential medicines remain issues in many countries.

The high cost of new essential medicines, particularly for cancer and other noncommunicable diseases, poses challenges for health systems across all income settings.

Global Health Observatory data from 2010–2019 show that the proportion of health facilities with a core set of relevant essential medicines available and affordable on a sustainable basis in selected low- and lower-middle-income countries ranged from 8% to 41%.

Medicines account for 20–60% of health spending in developing countries, with up to 90% of the population purchasing medicines through out-of-pocket payments, making medicines the largest family expenditure item after food. This means that medicines are unaffordable for large sections of the global population and are a major burden on government budgets.

Antimicrobial resistance is threatening the effectiveness of many essential antibiotics, necessitating careful stewardship.

sections.heading: History
sections.text:
The first WHO Model List of Essential Medicines was published in 1977 and included about 200 medicines. It was seen as a major revolution in public health, highlighting that some medicines are more important than others.

In 2007, the first Model List of Essential Medicines for Children (EMLc) was published in recognition of the unique needs of children. This was a major achievement, particularly in promoting research into medicines for children and the development of child-friendly formulations.

Over the years, the Model Lists have expanded in scope and complexity, reflecting advances in medical science, and changing global health priorities.

sections.heading: Update process
sections.text:
The WHO Model List is reviewed and updated every two years following a well-established, rigorous, transparent and evidence-based process.

Requests for changes to the WHO Model List, (such as the addition of new medicines or formulations, removal of medicines or formulations, or expanding the listing of a medicine to include a new indication), are made through an open application process. Applications may be submitted by anyone, including scientific researchers, academic institutions, non-governmental organizations, patient groups or networks, pharmaceutical companies and WHO technical departments.

Applications are reviewed by the WHO Expert Committee on Selection and Use of Essential Medicines, whose responsibility it is to consider the evidence presented and make recommendations to WHO regarding the requested changes.

Members of the Expert Committee are appointed by the WHO Director-General. They are required to have strong clinical and technical expertise in medicine evaluation and clinical use. Gender balance and equitable geographical representation are taken into consideration. Expert Committee members must disclose any circumstances that could result in a potential conflict of interest.

All applications received for consideration by the Expert Committee are published on the WHO website for public review and comment. Comments received on the applications, application reviews provided by Expert Committee members, and comments from WHO technical departments are also published on the website for full transparency.

This transparent, evidence-based process ensures that the WHO Model List remains a credible and valuable tool for guiding medicine selection and use globally.

sections.heading: Evolution of the WHO Model List
sections.text:
The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines has evolved significantly since its inception, reflecting its relevance to all countries, not just those with limited resources.

Since the first Model List in 1977, the number and scope of essential medicines included in the Model List have grown. Medicines requiring specialized medical care have been introduced, such as lung surfactants for newborn babies, targeted cancer treatments and medicines for multiple sclerosis. The Model List has also included more treatments for chronic and noncommunicable diseases, reflecting the changing global disease burden and ageing populations.

While the cost of a medicine is a consideration in the selection process, a high absolute cost of a medicine does not necessarily prevent it from being added to the WHO Model List if it otherwise meets the required selection criteria. Since 2002, affordability has evolved from being a precondition of listing a medicine on the Model list to being a consequence. Listing a medicine on the Model List is one step in a series of actions that can lead to lower costs, better affordability and greater access.

In 2017, in response to the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance, the WHO Model List introduced the AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) classification of antibiotics. The AWaRe classification guides the empiric use of essential antibiotics for more than 30 clinical infections in community and hospital settings. It has formed the basis of broader guidance for optimal antibiotic prescribing and use, supporting antimicrobial stewardship (5) .

sections.heading: WHO response
sections.text:
WHO continues to work to improve global access to essential medicines, regularly updating the WHO Model Lists of Essential Medicines and providing technical support to Member States to support them in implementing the 2014 World Health Assembly Resolution on Access to essential medicines (WHA 67.22).

Improving access and affordability of essential medicines forms an important part of WHO’s broader efforts to improve access and affordability of all essential health products – including medicines, assistive technologies, in vitro diagnostics, medical devices, and vaccines – as a key strategy for supporting countries to attain the goal of universal health coverage.

To achieve this, WHO has developed a range of guidance, tools and resources to support countries in the selection and use of essential medicines and other health products. Together with other WHO activities, such as prequalification of medical products and WHO guidelines, these efforts help to ensure evidence-based guidance is available for countries to make informed decisions for their national medicines policies, and selection and use of medicines for national essential medicines lists.

sections.heading: 重要事实
sections.text:
• 基本药物满足人们的重点医疗保健需求。

• 基本药物应随时可得、负担得起和质量有保证。

• 世卫组织每两年发布一次《基本药物标准清单》，以指导各国制定和更新国家基本药物清单。

• 世卫组织根据公共卫生相关性、有关益处和危害的证据并考虑成本、负担能力和其他相关因素来选择基本药物。

• 全球150多个国家根据世卫组织的标准清单制定了本国基本药物清单。

• 2025年版世卫组织《基本药物标准清单》包括520多种药物（含374种儿童药品）。

sections.heading: 概述
sections.text:
基本药物是有效安全地满足人们的重点医疗保健需求的药物。世卫组织根据公共卫生相关性、有关益处和危害的证据并考虑成本、负担能力和其他相关因素来选择基本药物。

正常运作的卫生系统应始终提供足够数量的基本药物，以满足患者需要。这些药物应当以适合预期用途和患者的适当剂型提供，质量有保证，且个人和卫生系统都负担得起。

虽然基本药物满足广泛的全球卫生需求，但它们在全球现有药物总数中只占很小比例。使用数量有限的精心挑选的药物可以改善供应，改进处方实践并降低成本。

自1977年以来，世卫组织每两年发布一次《基本药物标准清单》。

sections.heading: 影响和实施
sections.text:
全球150多个国家根据世卫组织的标准清单制定了本国基本药物清单。基本药物清单是公共部门采购和供应药品、报销和保险计划、药品捐赠和本地生产的依据(1)。基本药物概念如得到适当实施，可有助于改善健康结果，并在实现全民健康覆盖方面取得进展。基本药物的概念已在许多国家和区域得到成功实施。研究表明，基本药物清单有助于增加基本药物相对于非基本药物的供应(2)，提高可及性(3)，改善处方和护理质量，并节约成本(4)。

基本药物的概念可以适应各种卫生保健系统、环境和收入水平。通过集中注意数量有限的精心挑选的药品，各国可以改善供应，促进更合理的处方做法，更好地控制成本，同时确保获得基本药品。

sections.heading: 挑战
sections.text:
尽管取得了进展，但在确保普遍获得基本药物方面仍然存在挑战。在许多国家，基本药物的可得性和可负担性仍然成问题。

新的基本药物（特别是治疗癌症和其他非传染性疾病的基本药物）费用高昂，对所有收入环境的卫生系统都构成挑战。

全球卫生观察站 2010-2019年的数据显示，选定低收入和中低收入国家拥有一套可持续提供和负担得起的核心基本药物的卫生设施所占比例从8%到41%不等。

药品占发展中国家卫生支出的20-60%，高达90%的人口自费购买药品，使药品成为仅次于食品的最大家庭支出项目。这意味着全球很大部分人口负担不起，药品也成为政府预算的主要负担。

抗微生物药物耐药性正威胁着许多基本抗生素的有效性，需要谨慎管理。

sections.heading: 历史
sections.text:
第一版世卫组织《基本药物标准清单》于1977年发布，包括约200种药物。它被视为公共卫生领域的一场重大革命，突出表明某些药物比其他药物更重要。

世卫组织认识到儿童的独特需求，2007年发布第一版《儿童基本药物标准清单》。这是一项重大成就，特别是对于促进研究儿科用药和开发儿童友好配方而言。

多年来，《标准清单》的范围和复杂性不断扩大，反映了医学的进步和全球卫生重点的变化。

sections.heading: 更新过程
sections.text:
世卫组织《基本药物标准清单》每两年经过一个完善、严格、透明和循证的程序进行审查和更新。

修改清单的请求（如增加新的药物或制剂、删除药物或制剂，或扩大药物清单以包括新的适应症）通过公开申请程序提出。任何人都可以提出申请，包括科研人员、学术机构、非政府组织、患者团体或网络、制药公司和世卫组织技术部门。

申请由世卫组织基本药物的选择和使用专家委员会审查。该委员会负责审议所提交的证据，并就所要求的修改向世卫组织提出建议。

专家委员会成员由世卫组织总干事任命。他们要在药物评价和临床使用方面具有较强临床和技术专长。也会考虑性别均衡和公平地域代表性。专家委员会成员必须披露任何可能导致潜在利益冲突的情况。

所有提交专家委员会审议的申请都公布在世卫组织网站上，供公众查阅和评论。收到的相关评论、专家委员会成员提供的审查意见以及世卫组织技术部门的评论也在网站上公布，以实现充分透明。

这一基于证据的透明过程确保世卫组织《基本药物标准清单》仍然是指导全球药物选择和使用的可靠而宝贵的工具。

sections.heading: 世界卫生组织《基本药物标准清单》的演变
sections.text:
世卫组织《基本药物标准清单》自问世以来有了很大的发展。它对所有国家都有现实意义，而不仅仅是对那些资源有限的国家。

自1977年第一版《标准清单》以来，清单所列基本药物的数量和范围不断扩大。清单已纳入需要专门医疗护理的药品，如新生儿肺表面活性剂、有针对性的癌症治疗和多发性硬化症药物。清单还纳入了更多慢性病和非传染性疾病的治疗方法。这种变化体现了全球疾病负担的变化和人口老龄化。

虽然费用是选择过程中的一个考虑因素，但如果某种药物在其他方面符合既定选择标准，其绝对费用高并不一定妨碍将其列入《标准清单》。2002年以来，负担能力已从将药物列入标准清单的先决条件演变为后果。将一种药物列入标准清单是一系列行动中的一个步骤，这些行动可以降低成本，提高可负担性和增加获得机会。

2017年，为应对日益严重的抗微生物药物耐药性威胁，世卫组织《基本药物标准清单》引入了抗生素的可用、慎用、备用分类。该分类指导社区和医院环境中30多种临床感染的基本抗生素的经验性使用。它已成为最佳抗生素处方和使用的更广泛指导的基础，支持抗微生物药物管理(5)。

sections.heading: 世卫组织的应对
sections.text:
世卫组织继续努力改善全球基本药物的可及性，定期更新 世卫组织《基本药物标准清单》 ，并向会员国提供技术支持，以支持它们执行2014年世界卫生大会关于获得基本药物的决议(WHA67.22)。

改善基本药物的可及性和可负担性是世卫组织更广泛努力的一个重要组成部分，涵盖所有基本卫生产品（包括药品、辅助技术、体外诊断、医疗器械和疫苗）。这是支持各国实现全民健康覆盖目标的关键策略。

为此，世卫组织制定了一系列指导文件、工具和资源，以支持各国选择和使用基本药物和其他卫生产品。这些努力与世卫组织的其他活动，如医疗产品预认证和世卫组织指南相关活动，有助于确保各国获得循证指导，从而就其国家药物政策以及国家基本药物清单中的药物选择和使用做出知情决定。

sections.heading: Key facts
sections.text:
• Health literacy represents the personal knowledge and competencies that accumulate through daily activities, social interactions and across generations.

• Health literacy is mediated by the organizational structures and availability of resources that enable people to access, understand, appraise and use information and services in ways that promote and maintain good health and well-being for themselves and those around them – often described as organizational health literacy.

• In the United States of America, for example, health literacy is a stronger predictor of an individual’s health status than income, employment status, education level and racial or ethnic group (1) .

• Even in economically advanced countries in Europe , many children, adolescents and adults have limited health literacy skills (2) .

• According to surveys in the WHO European Region , population health literacy follows a social gradient and can further reinforce existing inequalities (2) .

• Health literacy is a determinant of health.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Health literacy means being able to access, understand, appraise and use information and services in ways that promote and maintain good health and well-being.

Health literacy means more than being able to access web sites, read pamphlets and follow prescribed health-seeking behaviours. It includes the ability to think critically about, as well as the ability to interact and express personal and societal needs for promoting health.

WHO defines health literacy as “representing the personal knowledge and competencies that accumulate through daily activities, social interactions and across generations. Personal knowledge and competencies are mediated by the organizational structures and availability of resources that enable people to access, understand, appraise, and use information and services in ways that promote and maintain good health and well-being for themselves and those around them.”

sections.heading: Why is it important to improve health literacy?
sections.text:
Health literacy requires inclusive and equitable access to quality education and life-long learning. Health literacy is shaped by a wide range of societal factors and is, therefore, not the sole responsibility of individuals to develop and maintain. All information providers, including government, civil society and health services should enable access to trustworthy information in a form that is understandable and actionable for all people. These social resources for health literacy include regulation of the information environment and media (oral, print, broadcast and digital) in which people obtain access to and use health information.

By improving people’s access to understandable and trustworthy health information and their capacity to use it effectively, health literacy is critical to both empowering people to make decisions about personal health, and in enabling their engagement in collective health promotion action to address the determinants of health.

sections.heading: Social benefits to high health literacy rates
sections.text:
Improving health literacy in populations provides the foundation on which citizens are enabled to:

• play an active role in improving their own health

• engage successfully with community action for health

• hold governments accountable for addressing health and health equity.

Meeting the health literacy needs of the most disadvantaged and marginalized societies can accelerate progress in reducing inequities in health and beyond. Efforts to raise health literacy will be crucial in achieving 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It is critical to transforming health systems to provide quality, people-centred, and equitable care.

sections.heading: Health literacy and existing inequalities
Improving health literacy
sections.text:
Strategies and interventions are recommended that increase both organizational and personal health literacy.

• Organizational health literacy can be promoted by improving training and organizational processes including strengthening communication, informed decision-making, and access to culturally and linguistically appropriate health information and services.

• Professional health literacy is an essential part of an organization’s responsiveness towards patients' health literacy and communication needs. It can be addressed through regular training of healthcare and education professionals.

• Personal health literacy may be strengthened by accurate, timely and appropriate health and science information as well as by the implementation of a health promoting educational curricula from an early age at home, in kindergartens, at schools through university level and as part of adult education.

• Assessing health literacy in populations and communities can guide policy development and intervention design to strengthen health literacy development in timely and relevant ways depending on needs.

sections.heading: WHO response
sections.text:
WHO promotes and improves health literacy by providing technical support and guidance to Members States to ensure effective management and promotion of health literacy at personal, organizational and systemic levels. To achieve this, WHO supports Members States to improve their reporting systems to accurately assess the extent of limited health literacy, including adapting global measurement instruments, and provides training for capacity building to promote health literacy. Reporting systems enable the creation of population data, and this evidence can be used to inform decisions at all levels, including for individuals, populations, capacity building of professionals, and systems. It also allows the collection of evidence on changes and enables responses to changing needs and circumstances. These efforts ensure that health literacy initiatives are robust, comprehensive, and tailored to meet the needs of populations worldwide. As a result, individuals and communities can make more informed decisions, organizations can better support individual and community health needs, and health care systems are strengthened, ultimately fostering better health outcomes and equity.

References

• Weiss Health literacy and patient safety: help patients understand. Manual for clinicians: Health literacy and patient safety: Help patients understand (hhvna.com)

• Health literacy in Europe: comparative results of the European health literacy survey (HLS-EU) - PMC (nih.gov)

sections.heading: 重要事实
sections.text:
• 健康素养指通过日常活动、社交活动和代际交流积累的个人知识和能力。

• 健康素养受组织结构和可用资源的影响，这些结构和资源可帮助人们获取、理解、评价和使用信息和服务从而促进和维护自身及周围人的健康与福祉，这通常被称为组织健康素养。

• 例如，在美利坚合众国，健康素养比收入、就业状况、教育水平和种族或族裔群体更能预测个人的健康状况 (1) 。

• 即使 在欧洲 的经济发达国家，许多儿童、青少年和成人的健康素养技能也有限 (2) 。

• 根据 对世卫组织欧洲区域的调查 ，人口健康素养呈现社会梯度变化，并可能进一步加剧现有的不平等 (2) 。

• 健康素养是健康的一个决定因素。

sections.heading: 概述
sections.text:
健康素养意味着能够获取、理解、评价和使用信息和服务从而促进和维护自身及周围人的健康与福祉。

健康素养不仅仅意味着能够访问网站、阅读手册和遵循规定的求医行为。它还包括批判性思考能力，以及互动能力和表达对促进健康的个人和社会需求的能力。

关于健康素养的 世卫组织定义 是“通过日常活动、社交活动和代际交流积累的个人知识和能力。这种个人知识和能力受组织结构和可用资源的影响，这些结构和资源可帮助人们获取、理解、评价和使用信息和服务从而促进和维护自身及周围人的健康与福祉。”

sections.heading: 为什么必须提高健康素养？
sections.text:
健康素养需要包容和公平地获得优质教育和终身学习机会。健康素养受广泛的社会因素影响，因此，发展和维持健康素养不仅仅是个人的责任。所有信息提供者，包括政府、民间社会和卫生服务机构，都应该为所有人提供可靠、可理解和可用的信息。这些促进健康素养的社会资源包括对人们获取和使用健康信息的信息环境和媒体（口头、印刷、广播和数字媒体）进行监管。

健康素养可使人们更好地获取可理解和可靠的健康信息并提高人们有效使用这些信息的能力，因此对增强人们的能力至关重要，不仅使人们能够就个人健康做出决定，而且能够参与集体促进健康行动以解决健康问题的决定因素。

sections.heading: 高健康素养水平的社会效益
sections.text:
提高人口的健康素养可奠定基础使公民能够：

• 在改善自身健康方面发挥积极作用

• 成功参与社区健康促进行动

• 要求政府负责解决健康和健康公平问题。

满足最弱势和边缘化社群的健康素养需求可以加速减少健康及其他领域的不平等现象。努力提高健康素养对于实现《2030年可持续发展议程》至关重要。健康素养对于改革卫生系统以提供优质、以人为本和公平的护理必不可少。

sections.heading: 健康素养和既有的不平等现象
sections.text:
健康素养与年龄、性别、受教育程度、收入和职业、贫困、种族/少数民族地位、识字和语言能力、健康保险覆盖率和自我报告的健康状况有关。不同人群和环境内部及之间存在差异。这些差异因各种差距而加剧，可能影响人们培养和使用健康素养的难易程度，以及对优质可靠信息和服务的获取。在制定卫生政策和分配资源时，必须考虑到这些差距。即使是阅读能力强、善于使用数字的人，在以下情况中也会面临健康素养问题：

• 不熟悉医学术语或自己身体的运作方式；

• 必须解释统计数据，评估影响其健康和安全的风险和利益；

• 被诊断出患有严重疾病，感到恐惧和困惑；

• 处于压力之下，必须做出重要的健康决定；

• 自身健康状况需要进行复杂的自我护理；或

• 就影响社区健康的问题进行投票，并依赖不熟悉的技术信息，这可能会进一步加剧性别和健康公平问题。

这使得健康素养成为健康和健康行为的一个重要决定因素。与此同时，也出现了新的健康决定因素，并有可能扩大不平等差距。例如，健康问题的数字决定因素和商业决定因素等。

sections.heading: 提高健康素养
sections.text:
建议采取能提高组织和个人健康素养的策略和干预措施。

• 可以通过改进培训和组织流程来促进 组织健康素养 ，包括加强沟通、知情决策以及获取适合文化和语言需要的健康信息和服务。

• 专业健康素养 是组织响应患者的健康素养和沟通需求的必要组成部分，可以通过定期培训卫生保健和教育专业人员来培养。

• 可以通过准确、及时和适当的健康和科学信息，以及通过从小在家里、幼儿园、学校和大学并作为成人教育的一部分实施健康促进教育课程来加强 个人健康素养 。

• 在人群和社区中 评估健康素养 可以指导制定政策和设计干预措施，从而根据需要及时有意义地加强健康素养。

sections.heading: 世卫组织的应对
sections.text:
世卫组织通过向会员国提供技术支持和指导来促进和提高健康素养，以确保在个人、组织和系统层面有效管理和促进健康素养。为实现这一目标，世卫组织支持会员国改进其报告系统以准确评估健康素养的有限程度，包括调整应用全球衡量工具，此外还提供能力建设培训，以促进健康素养。报告系统有助于创建人口数据，这方面证据可用于为各个层面，包括个人、人群、专业人员的能力建设以及系统等层面的决策提供信息。此外，还允许收集有关变化的证据，并能够应对不断变化的需求和情况。这些努力可确保促进健康素养的各种举措稳健、全面且有针对性，以满足全球人口的需求。由此，个人和社区可以做出更明智的决定，组织可以更好地支持个人和社区的健康需求，卫生保健系统可得到加强，最终可促进实现更好的健康结果和公平。

参考文献

• Weiss Health literacy and patient safety: help patients understand. Manual for clinicians: Health literacy and patient safety: Help patients understand (hhvna.com)

• Health literacy in Europe: comparative results of the European health literacy survey (HLS-EU) - PMC (nih.gov)

sections.heading: Overview
The benefits of rehabilitation
sections.text:
Rehabilitation can reduce the impact of a broad range of health conditions, including diseases (acute or chronic), illnesses or injuries. It complements other health interventions, such as medical and surgical interventions, helping to facilitate recovery 
 and achieve the best outcome possible. In addition, rehabilitation can help to prevent, reduce or manage complications associated with many health conditions, such as in the context of spinal cord injury, stroke, or fractures.

Rehabilitation helps to minimize or slow down the disabling effects of chronic health conditions, such as cardiovascular disease, cancer and diabetes by equipping people with self-management strategies and the assistive products they require, or by addressing 
 pain or other complications. As such, it contributes to healthy ageing.

Rehabilitation is an investment, with cost benefits for both the individuals and society. It can help to avoid costly hospitalization, reduce hospital length of stay, and prevent re-admissions. As rehabilitation also enables individuals to engage in or 
 return to work and employment, or to remain independent at home, it minimizes the need for financial or caregiver support.

Rehabilitation is an important part of universal health coverage and is a key strategy for achieving Sustainable Development Goal 3 – “Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages”.

sections.heading: Misconceptions about rehabilitation
sections.text:
Rehabilitation is not only for people with disabilities or long-term or physical impairments. Rather, rehabilitation is an essential health service for anyone with an acute or chronic health condition, impairment or injury that limits functioning, and 
 as such should be available for anyone who needs it.

Rehabilitation is not a luxury health service that is available only for those who can afford it. Nor is it an optional service to try only when other interventions to prevent or cure a health condition fail.

For the full extent of the social, economic and health benefits of rehabilitation to be realized, timely, high quality and affordable rehabilitation interventions should be available to all. In many cases, this means starting rehabilitation as soon as 
 a health condition is noted and continuing to deliver rehabilitation alongside other health interventions.

sections.heading: Unmet global need for rehabilitation
Rehabilitation in emergencies
sections.text:
Natural hazards such as earthquakes or disease outbreaks and human induced hazards including conflict, terrorism or industrial accidents can generate overwhelming rehabilitation needs as a result of injury or illness. They also simultaneously disrupt 
 existing services and have the greatest impact on the most vulnerable populations and the weakest health systems.

While the important role of rehabilitation in emergencies is recognized in clinical and humanitarian guidelines, it is rarely considered as part of health system preparedness and early response. The result is that pre-existing limitations in rehabilitation 
 services are magnified, health service delivery is less efficient, and people directly affected are at risk of increased impairment and disability.

sections.heading: WHO response
sections.text:
A health system strengthening approach is needed to ensure that rehabilitation services can reach all who need them. This involves making rehabilitation part of all levels of care, including primary care, and ensuring it is incorporated as part of universal health coverage.

WHO’s work is guided by the resolution on Strengthening rehabilitation in health systems adopted at the Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly implemented through the Rehabilitation 2030 initiative as requested by the resolution.

WHO’s work focuses on providing technical support to Member States in the areas of:

• Rehabilitation leadership and governance Rehabilitation in health systems.

• Rehabilitation financing Rehabilitation in health financing: opportunities on the way to universal health coverage.

• Rehabilitation health information systems Routine health information systems- rehabilitation toolkit.

• Rehabilitation service delivery Basic rehabilitation package clinical resource Access to rehabilitation in primary health care: an ongoing challenge.

• Rehabilitation workforce Rehabilitation competency framework Guide for rehabilitation workforce evaluation Strengthening rehabilitation research and evidence Rehabilitation Need Estimator Health Policy and Systems Research Agenda for Rehabilitation WHO bulletin.

• Strengthening rehabilitation in emergencies Strengthening rehabilitation in health emergency preparedness, readiness, response and resilience: policy brief Minimum technical standards and recommendations for rehabilitation in emergency medical teams .

WHO is also working to strengthen rehabilitation advocacy, through the World Rehabilitation Alliance .

sections.heading: 重要事实
sections.text:
• 与促进良好健康、预防疾病、治疗和姑息治疗服务一样，康复服务是全民健康覆盖的重要内容。

• 康复服务有助于儿童、成人或老人在日常活动中尽可能自立，能够参与教育、工作和娱乐活动，并在生活中发挥有益的作用，如照顾家人。

• 目前全球估计有 24 亿人患有可能通过康复服务获得改善的健康问题。

• 由于人口健康和人口特点的变化，全世界对康复服务的需求预计将进一步增加。例如，人们寿命延长，但慢性病和残疾在增多等。

• 目前，康复需求大多没有得到满足。在一些低收入和中等收入国家，超过 50% 的人得不到所需要的康复服务。冲突、灾害和疫情等紧急情况导致康复需求迅速增加，同时也扰乱了康复服务。

• 康复服务是全民健康覆盖的一项重要内容，是实现可持续发展目标 3 （ “确保健康生活，促进所有年龄段的人的健康” ）的一项关键策略。

sections.heading: 概述
sections.text:
康复服务的定义是“一套旨在优化有健康问题者的身体功能和减轻其残疾，改善其与环境的互动的干预措施”。

简而言之，康复服务有助于儿童、成人或老人在日常活动中尽可能自立，能够参与教育、工作和娱乐活动，并在生活中发挥有益的作用，如照顾家人。也就是说，与患者及其家人合作对付基础健康问题及其症状，改变周围环境以更好地满足需求，使用辅助器具，进行训练以加强自我管理，并调整任务以便能以更安全和独立的方式加以执行。这些策略合在一起可帮助个人克服在思考、视力、听觉、沟通、饮食或走动方面的困难。

任何人都可能在生命中某一时刻点需要康复服务，例如在受伤、手术、生病之后，或者因为功能随着年龄增长而衰退。

康复服务包括：

• 说话和语言训练，以改善一个人在脑损伤后的沟通。

• 体育锻炼，以提高中风或帕金森病患者的肌肉力量、自主运动和平衡。

• 调整老年人的居家环境，增强其在家中的安全性和独立性，降低跌倒风险。

• 教给心脏病患者安全运动的方式。

• 帮助截肢者为使用假肢做好准备，并制作、安装和改装假肢。

• 在烧伤手术后，采用定位和夹板技术，协助皮肤愈合，减少肿胀，并恢复运动功能。

• 为脑瘫患儿开处减轻痉挛的药物。

• 为脊髓损伤后出现情绪困扰的患者提供心理治疗。

• 为精神分裂症、自闭症谱系障碍或智力残障患者提供社交技能培训。

• 训练丧失视力者使用白色拐杖。

• 与重症监护患者一起努力改善其呼吸，预防并发症并加快重病后的恢复。

康复服务在很大程度上因人而异，也就是说，需根据个人的目标和偏好选择适当的干预措施。可在许多不同场所提供康复服务，例如医院的住院部或门诊部、门诊理疗或作业治疗中心，以及社区环境，例如家中、学校或工作场所等。

康复服务人员由各类卫生工作者包括但不局限于理疗师、作业治疗师、言谈和语言治疗师及听力学家、矫形师和假肢师、临床心理学家、物理医学和康复医生以及康复护士组成。许多其他卫生工作者，如全科医生、外科医生和社区卫生工作者也可在一个人的康复中发挥重要作用。

sections.heading: 康复服务的益处
sections.text:
康复服务可以减轻（急性或慢性）疾患或伤害等各种健康问题的影响，并可补充其他卫生干预措施，如医疗和外科干预措施，有助于促进恢复并取得尽可能最佳结果。此外，康复服务可以帮助预防、减少或管理与许多健康问题相关的并发症，例如在脊髓损伤、中风或骨折的情况下。

康复服务有助于最大限度减轻或减缓慢性疾病（如心血管疾病、癌症和糖尿病）的严重影响，为人们提供自我管理策略和所需的辅助器具，或解决疼痛或其他并发症，因此，可促进健康的老龄化。

康复服务是一项投资，能为个人和社会带来成本效益。它可以帮助避免昂贵的住院费用，缩短住院时间，并避免今后重新入院治疗。由于康复服务还可使个人能够从事或重返工作和就业，或能够在家中自立，因此可最大限度减少对经济支持或照护人员的需求。

康复服务是全民健康覆盖的一项重要内容，是实现可持续发展目标3（“确保健康生活，促进所有年龄段的人的健康”）的一项关键策略。

sections.heading: 对康复服务的误解
sections.text:
康复服务不仅适合残疾人或有长期障碍或有生理障碍的人。康复服务是对任何有急性或慢性健康问题的人以及有限制身体功能的障碍或损伤的人的一项基本卫生服务，因此，任何有需要的人都应获得此种服务。

康复服务不是一种奢侈的卫生服务，只有那些负担得起的人才可以享受。也不是可有可无，不是只有在其他防治措施失败的情况下才尝试提供的服务。

为充分实现康复服务的社会、经济和健康效益，人人都应能获得及时、高质量和负担得起的康复措施。在许多情况下，这意味着一旦发现有健康问题，就应立即开始康复治疗，并与其他卫生干预措施一起持续提供康复服务。

sections.heading: 未获满足的全球康复需求
sections.text:
目前全球估计有24亿人患有可能通过康复服务获得改善的健康问题。随着全世界人口健康和特点的变化，这一估计的康复需求在未来几年将只会增加。人们寿命越来越长，预计到2050年，60岁以上的人数将翻一番。越来越多的人患有糖尿病、中风和癌症等慢性疾病。同时，在目前，伤害和儿童发育问题（如脑瘫）的发生率居高不下。这些健康问题可能会影响个人运作，加剧残疾程度。康复服务有助于减少残疾。

在世界许多地区，日益增长的对康复服务的需求在很大程度上没有得到满足。在一些低收入和中等收入国家需要康复服务的人中，有一半以上的人得不到康复服务。

全球康复需求未得到满足是多种因素造成的，例如：

• 缺乏国家康复服务重点、资金、政策和计划。

• 在城区以外缺乏康复服务，且等待时间过长。

• 自付额过高，资金渠道缺乏或不足。

• 缺乏训练有素的康复服务专业人员，在许多低收入和中等收入国家中，每100万人口中熟练的康复服务专业人员不到10人。

• 缺乏资源，包括缺乏辅助技术、设备和消耗品。

• 关于康复服务的研究和数据不足。

• 向康复服务转诊的途径低效，且未获得充分使用。

sections.heading: 紧急情况中的康复服务
sections.text:
地震或疫情等自然灾害以及人为灾害（包括冲突、恐怖主义或工业事故）造成人们受伤或生病，进而带来巨大的康复需求。同时，它们还会扰乱现有服务，对最脆弱的人群和最薄弱的卫生系统造成最大影响。

临床指南和人道主义准则均确认在紧急情况中康复服务的重要作用，但很少将康复服务视为卫生系统防范和早期应对工作的一部分。结果，康复服务中本就存在的局限被放大，卫生服务交付效率低下，直接受影响的人面临较高的损伤和残疾风险。

sections.heading: 世卫组织的应对
sections.text:
需要采取卫生系统强化方法，确保所有需要的人都能获得康复服务。康复服务应成为包括初级保健在内的各级卫生保健服务的一部分，并应确保将其纳入全民健康覆盖的范围。

世卫组织根据 第七十六届世界卫生大会通过的关于加强卫生系统康复服务的决议 ，并按照该决议的要求，努力落实“康复2030”倡议并开展了有关工作。

世卫组织的工作重点是在以下领域向会员国提供技术支持：

• 康复领域的领导作用和治理工作 卫生系统中的康复工作

• 康复服务筹资 为卫生领域康复服务筹集资金：利用机会实现全民健康覆盖

• 加强康复专题卫生信息系统 常规卫生信息系统 - 康复工具包

• 提供康复服务 一揽子康复干预措施 基本康复服务临床资源 获得初级保健康复服务：一项持续挑战

sections.heading: Fact sheet
sections.text: A fall is defined as an event which results in a person coming to rest inadvertently on the ground or floor or other lower level. Fall-related injuries may be fatal or non-fatal (1) though most are non-fatal. For example, of children in the People's Republic of China, for every death due to a fall, there are 4 cases of permanent disability, 13 cases requiring hospitalization for more than 10 days, 24 cases requiring hospitalization for 1–9 days and 690 cases seeking medical care or missing work/school.

sections.heading: The problem
sections.text:
Globally, falls are a major public health problem. An estimated 684 000 fatal falls occur each year, making it the second leading cause of unintentional injury death, after road traffic injuries. Over 80% of fall-related fatalities occur in low- and middle-income countries, with regions of the Western Pacific and South East Asia accounting for 60% of these deaths. In all regions of the world, death rates are highest among adults over the age of 60 years.

Though not fatal, approximately 37.3 million falls severe enough to require medical attention occur each year. Globally, falls are responsible for over 38 million DALYs (disability-adjusted life years) lost each year (2), and result in more years lived with disability than transport injury, drowning, burns and poisoning combined.

While nearly 40% of the total DALYs lost due to falls worldwide occurs in children, this measurement may not accurately reflect the impact of fall-related disabilities for older individuals who have fewer life years to lose. In addition, those individuals who fall and suffer a disability, particularly older people, are at a major risk for subsequent long-term care and institutionalization.

The financial costs from fall-related injuries are substantial. For people aged 65 years or older, the average health system cost per fall injury in the Republic of Finland and Australia are US$ 3611 and US$ 1049 respectively. Evidence from Canada suggests the implementation of effective prevention strategies with a subsequent 20% reduction in the incidence of falls among children under 10 years of age could create a net savings of over US$ 120 million each year.

sections.heading: Who is at risk?
sections.text: While all people who fall are at risk of injury, the age, gender and health of the individual can affect the type and severity of injury.

sections.heading: Age
sections.text:
Age is one of the key risk factors for falls. Older people have the highest risk of death or serious injury arising from a fall and the risk increases with age. For example, in the United States of America, 20–30% of older people who fall suffer moderate to severe injuries such as bruises, hip fractures, or head trauma. This risk level may be in part due to physical, sensory, and cognitive changes associated with ageing, in combination with environments that are not adapted for an ageing population.

Another high risk group is children. Childhood falls occur largely as a result of their evolving developmental stages, innate curiosity in their surroundings, and increasing levels of independence that coincide with more challenging behaviours commonly referred to as ‘risk taking’. While inadequate adult supervision is a commonly cited risk factor, the circumstances are often complex, interacting with poverty, sole parenthood, and particularly hazardous environments.

sections.heading: Gender
Prevention
sections.text:
A range of interventions exist to prevent falls across the life-course. These include, but are not limited to, the following:

For children and adolescents

• Parenting programmes for low-income and marginalized families

• Providing parents with information about child fall risks and supporting them to reduce these risks around the home

For workers

• Enforcement of more stringent workplace safety regulations in high risk occupations such as the construction industry

• Multicomponent workplace safety programmes

For older people

• Gait, balance and functional training

• Tai Chi

• Home assessment and modifications

• Reduction or withdrawal of psychotropic drugs

• Multifactorial interventions (individual fall-risk assessments followed by tailored interventions and referrals to address identified risks)

• Vitamin D supplements for those who are Vitamin D deficient

In addition to the interventions mentioned above there are others that are considered prudent to implement despite the fact that they may never have a body of research to support them. This is because the nature of the intervention is such that they are unlikely to be the subject of high-quality research studies either due to difficulties in performing the required research, or because the interventions seem so basic or fundamental that research is not deemed necessary. Examples of such interventions include:

• Fence off, or otherwise restrict access to dangerous areas

• Promote policies and playground standards requiring soft play surfaces and restricted fall heights

• Functioning occupational health and safety systems

• Harnesses, restraint systems, fall arrest systems and safe scaffolding for those working at heights

• Requiring landlords to make necessary modifications to homes and the enforcement of building standards

• Improved accessibility of neighbourhoods and public spaces e.g. pavements

• Ensure adequate staff-to-resident ratios in residential care facilities

(1) Within the WHO Global Health Estimates, fall-related deaths and non-fatal injuries exclude falls due to assault and self-harm; falls from animals, burning buildings, transport vehicles; and falls into fire, water and machinery.

(2) The disability-adjusted life year (DALY) extends the concept of potential years of life lost due to premature death to include equivalent years of “healthy” life lost by virtue of being in states of poor health or disability.

sections.heading: Fact sheet
sections.text: 跌倒系指导致一个人不慎落在地面或地板或其他低于其原先位置的表面上的事故。与跌倒有关的伤害可以是致命或非致命的伤害 (1) ，但大多数是非致命的伤害。例如，在中国儿童中，因跌倒导致的每一例死亡对应4例永久性残疾，13例需要住院治疗10天以上，24例需要住院治疗1-9天，690例需要医治或缺勤/缺课。

sections.heading: 问题
sections.text:
在世界各地，跌伤是一重要公共卫生问题。据估计，每年发生68.4万例致命跌伤，使之成为仅次于道路交通伤害的第二大非故意伤害死亡原因。80%以上与跌倒有关的死亡发生在低收入和中等收入国家，其中西太平洋区域和东南亚区域占60%。在世界所有区域，60岁以上成年人死亡率最高。

即使不致命，每年仍约有3730万例跌伤严重到需要进行治疗。全球每年因跌倒而损失3800多万残疾调整生命年 (2) ，致使伤残所致生命损失年数超过交通伤害、溺水、烧伤和中毒的总和。

虽然全世界因跌倒而损失的残疾调整生命年中几乎40%发生在儿童身上，但此衡量可能无法准确反映与跌倒相关的残疾对寿命年数较少的老年人的影响。此外，因跌倒而致残的人，尤其是老年人，随后需要长期护理和进收容机构的风险极大。

跌倒相关伤害的经济成本巨大。在芬兰和澳大利亚，65岁及以上者每一例跌伤的平均卫生系统费用分别为3611美元和1049美元。来自加拿大的证据表明，实施有效的预防策略，可使10岁以下儿童的跌伤发生率下降20%，每年可净节省1.2亿多美元。

sections.heading: 什么人有危险？
sections.text: 每个跌倒的人都有可能受伤，但因个人年龄、性别和健康状况的不同，受伤的类型和严重程度会有差异。

sections.heading: 年龄
sections.text:
年龄是跌倒的主要风险因素之一。老年人因跌倒而死亡或受重伤的风险最大，年龄越大，风险越高。例如，在美国，跌倒的老年人中20%-30%遭受中度至重度伤害，如擦伤、髋部骨折或头部创伤。导致这一风险的部分原因可能是身体、感官和认知方面出现老化，而同时环境也不能适应人口老龄化的需要。

另一个高危群体是儿童。儿童跌跤主要是其身体尚在发育阶段，对周围事物充满好奇，在独立性逐渐增强的同时会有较具挑战性的行为，通常称为“冒险”。尽管成年人监督不够是普遍提及的危险因素，但具体情况往往很复杂，与贫困、单亲，特别是危险环境等各种不利因素交织在一起。

sections.heading: 性别
sections.text:
在所有年龄组和区域，男女都有跌伤的风险。在一些国家，人们注意到男性更有可能死于跌伤，女性则多为非致命的跌伤。老年妇女和幼童尤其容易跌倒，伤势也更为严重。在世界范围内，男性死亡率和损失的残疾调整生命年一贯较高。男性中这一负担较重的原因可能包括冒险行为较多和职业危险程度更高。

其他风险因素包括：

• 高空作业或其他危险的工作条件；

• 酒精或药物使用；

• 社会经济因素，包括贫困、住房拥挤、单亲、母亲过于年轻；

• 患有神经性疾病、心脏病或其他致残性疾病等基础病症；

• 药物副作用、缺乏身体活动和丧失平衡，尤其多见于老年人；

• 行动能力、认知能力和视力不佳，尤其是在公共服务性机构，如养老院或长期护理设施中生活的人；

• 不安全环境，尤其对平衡能力差和视力不好的人而言。

sections.heading: 预防
sections.text:
有一系列干预措施可在生命全程预防跌伤。这些包括但不限于以下措施：

针对儿童和青少年

• 制定面向低收入和边缘化家庭的育儿规划；

• 向父母提供关于儿童跌倒风险的信息，并帮助他们在家中降低这些风险。

针对工作者

• 在建筑行业等高风险职业中执行更严格的工作场所安全法规；

• 制定多元化工作场所安全规划。

针对老年人

• 步态、平衡和功能训练；

• 太极拳；

• 家居评估和改造；

• 减少或停用精神药物；

• 多因素干预（评估个体跌倒风险，之后定制干预措施和转诊，以解决已确定的风险）；

• 为维生素D缺乏者提供维生素D补充剂。

除了上述干预措施之外，出于谨慎考虑还应实施另一些可能永远得不到研究支持的干预措施。事实上，这些干预措施由于其性质可能难以进行必要研究，或可能过于基本而认为不必要进行研究，因此不太可能成为高质量研究的对象。这类干预措施的例子包括：

• 隔离或以其他方式限制进入危险区域；

• 推广关于游戏场所的政策和标准，要求铺设软质场地和限制跌落高度；

• 正常运作的职业健康和安全系统；

• 高空作业人员的安全带、约束系统、防坠落系统和安全脚手架；

• 要求房主对房屋进行必要的改造并执行建筑标准；

• 改善街区和公共空间（如人行道）的可及性；

• 确保寄宿护理机构中员工与寄宿者的比率得当。

(1) 世卫组织全球卫生估计中与跌倒有关的死亡和非致命伤害数据，不包括因袭击和自残导致的跌伤，从动物身上、燃烧的建筑物、运输车辆上的坠落，以及跌入大火、水中和机械中的事故。

(2) 残疾调整生命年（DALY）扩大了由于过早死亡而可能丧失的生命年的概念，包括因健康状况不佳或残疾而丧失的等同“健康”生命年。

sections.heading: Key facts
sections.text:
• An estimated 180 000 deaths every year are caused by burns. The vast majority occur in low- and middle-income countries.

• Non-fatal burn injuries are a leading cause of morbidity.

• Burns occur mainly in the home and workplace.

• Burns are preventable.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A burn is an injury to the skin or other organic tissue primarily caused by heat or due to radiation, radioactivity, electricity, friction or contact with chemicals.

Thermal (heat) burns occur when some or all the cells in the skin or other tissues are destroyed by:

• hot liquids (scalds)

• hot solids (contact burns)

• flames (flame burns).

sections.heading: The problem
sections.text:
Burns are a global public health problem, accounting for an estimated 180 000 deaths annually. The majority of these occur in low- and middle-income countries and almost two thirds occur in the WHO African and South-East Asia Regions.

In many high-income countries, burn death rates have been decreasing, and the rate of child deaths from burns is currently over 7 times higher in low- and middle-income countries than in high-income countries.

Non-fatal burns are a leading cause of morbidity, including prolonged hospitalization, disfigurement and disability, often with resulting stigma and rejection.

• Burns are among the leading causes of disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) lost in low- and middle-income countries.

• Hospitalization for burns varies by country and is influenced by health service payment programmes, but among countries studied hospitalization trends are going towards shorter stays and an increased proportion of burns being treated in specialized burn centres (1).

sections.heading: Some country data
sections.text:
• In India, over 1 million people are moderately or severely burnt every year.

• Nearly 173 000 Bangladeshi children are moderately or severely burnt every year.

• In Bangladesh, Colombia, Egypt and Pakistan, 17% of children with burns have a temporary disability and 18% have a permanent disability.

• Burns are the second most common injury in rural Nepal, accounting for 5% of disabilities.

• In 2008, over 410 000 burn injuries occurred in the United States of America, with approximately 40 000 requiring hospitalization.

sections.heading: Economic impact
sections.text:
Direct care costs for burns vary widely but tend towards being generally expensive with a 2014 systematic review finding a mean total healthcare cost per burn patient of US$ 88 218 (range US$ 704–717 306).

In South Africa an estimated US$ 26 million is spent annually for care of burns from kerosene (paraffin) cookstove incidents. Indirect costs such as lost wages, prolonged care for deformities and emotional trauma, and commitment of family resources, also contribute to the socioeconomic impact.

sections.heading: Who is at risk? / Gender
sections.text:
Females have slightly higher rates of death from burns compared to males according to the most recent data. This contrasts with the usual injury pattern, where rates of injury for the various injury mechanisms tend to be higher in males than females.

The higher risk for females is associated with open fire cooking, or inherently unsafe cookstoves, which can ignite loose clothing. Open flames used for heating and lighting also pose risks, and self-directed or interpersonal violence are also factors (although understudied).

sections.heading: Age
sections.text: Along with adult women, children are particularly vulnerable to burns. Burns are the fifth most common cause of non-fatal childhood injuries. While a major risk is improper adult supervision, a considerable number of burn injuries in children result from child maltreatment.

sections.heading: Regional factors
sections.text:
There are important regional differences in burn rates.

• Children under 5 years of age in the WHO African Region have over 2 times the incidence of burn deaths than children under 5 years of age worldwide.

• Boys under 5 years of age living in low- and middle-income countries of the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region are almost 2 times as likely to die from burns as boys living in the WHO European Region.

• The incidence of burn injuries requiring medical care is nearly 20 times higher in the WHO Western Pacific Region than in the WHO Region of the Americas.

sections.heading: Socioeconomic factors
sections.text: People living in low- and middle-income countries are at higher risk for burns than people living in high-income countries. Within all countries however, burn risk correlates with socioeconomic status.

sections.heading: Other risk factors
In which settings do burns occur?
sections.text: Burns occur mainly in the home and workplace. Community surveys in Bangladesh and Ethiopia show that 80–90% of burns occur at home. Children and women are usually burned in domestic kitchens, from upset receptacles containing hot liquids or flames, or from cookstove explosions. Men are most likely to be burned in the workplace due to fire, scalds, chemical and electrical burns.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.text:
Burns are preventable. High-income countries have made considerable progress in lowering rates of burn deaths, through a combination of prevention strategies and improvements in the care of people affected by burns. Most of these advances in prevention and care have been incompletely applied in low- and middle-income countries. Increased efforts to do so would likely lead to significant reductions in rates of burn-related death and disability.

Prevention strategies should address the hazards for specific burn injuries, education for vulnerable populations and training of communities in first aid. An effective burn prevention plan should be multisectoral and include broad efforts to:

• improve awareness

• develop and enforce effective policy

• describe burden and identify risk factors

• set research priorities with promotion of promising interventions

• provide burn prevention programmes

• strengthen burn care

• strengthen capacities to carry out all the above.

The document A WHO plan for burn prevention and care discusses these 7 components in detail.

In addition, there are several specific recommendations for individuals, communities and public health officials to reduce burn risk.

• Enclose fires and limit the height of open flames in domestic environments.

• Promote safer cookstoves and less hazardous fuels and educate regarding loose clothing.

• Apply safety regulations to housing designs and materials and encourage home inspections.

• Improve the design of cookstoves, particularly with regard to stability and prevention of access by children.

• Lower the temperature in hot water taps.

• Promote fire safety education and the use of smoke detectors, fire sprinklers and fire-escape systems in homes.

• Promote the introduction of and compliance with industrial safety regulations, and the use of fire-retardant fabrics for children’s sleepwear.

• Avoid smoking in bed and encourage the use of child-resistant lighters.

• Promote legislation mandating the production of fire-safe cigarettes.

• Improve treatment of epilepsy, particularly in developing countries.

• Encourage further development of burn-care systems, including the training of health-care providers in the appropriate triage and management of people with burns.

• Support the development and distribution of fire-retardant aprons to be used while cooking around an open flame or kerosene stove.

sections.heading: First aid
sections.text: Basic guidance on first aid for burns is provided below.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.text:
• Stop the burning process by removing clothing and irrigating the burns.

• Extinguish flames by allowing the patient to roll on the ground, or by applying a blanket, or by using water or other fire-extinguishing liquids.

• Use cool running water to reduce the temperature of the burn.

• In chemical burns, remove or dilute the chemical agent by irrigating with large volumes of water.

• Wrap the patient in a clean cloth or sheet and transport to the nearest appropriate facility for medical care.

sections.heading: What not to do
sections.text:
• Do not start first aid before ensuring your own safety (switch off electrical current, wear gloves for chemicals etc.)

• Do not apply paste, oil, haldi (turmeric) or raw cotton to the burn.

• Do not apply ice because it deepens the injury.

• Avoid prolonged cooling with water because it will lead to hypothermia.

• Do not open blisters until topical antimicrobials can be applied, such as by a health-care provider.

• Do not apply any material directly to the wound as it might become infected.

• Avoid application of topical medication until the patient has been placed under appropriate medical care.

sections.heading: WHO response
sections.text:
WHO is promoting interventions that have been shown to be successful in reducing the incidence of burns.

The Organization is also supporting the development and use of a global burn registry for globally harmonized data collection on burns and increased collaboration between global and national networks to increase the number of effective programmes for burn prevention.

References

• Recent Trends in Burn Epidemiology Worldwide: A Systematic Review. Burns. 2017 Mar; 43(2): 249–257.

sections.heading: 要事实
sections.text:
• 据估计，每年有18万人死于烧伤。绝大多数发生在低收入和中等收入国家。

• 非致命烧伤是一项主要致病因素。

• 烧伤主要发生在家庭和工作场所。

• 烧伤可以预防。

sections.heading: 概述
sections.text:
烧伤是一种主要由高温引起，或由辐射、放射、电、摩擦或接触化学品而导致的皮肤或其它器官组织的损伤。

当皮肤中或其它组织中的部分或全部细胞被下列物质破坏时会发生热力（高温）烧伤：

• 高温液体（烫伤）。

• 高温固体（接触烧伤）。

• 火焰（灼伤）。

sections.heading: 问题
sections.text:
烧伤是一项全球性公共卫生问题，估计每年导致约18万例死亡。其中大部分发生在低收入和中等收入国家，约有三分之二发生在世卫组织非洲和东南亚区域。

许多高收入国家的烧伤死亡率不断降低。目前低收入和中等收入国家中死于烧伤的儿童比例是高收入国家的七倍以上。

非致命烧伤是一项主要致病因素，造成长期住院、毁容和残疾等，并往往导致患者受辱和遭受排斥。

• 烧伤是低收入和中等收入国家中残疾调整生命年损失的主要原因之一。

• 烧伤住院情况因国家而异，并受卫生服务支付计划的影响，但在所研究的国家中，住院时间趋于缩短，在专业烧伤中心接受治疗的比例出现上升 (1) 。

sections.heading: 一些国家的数据
sections.text:
• 在印度，每年有100多万人遭受中度或严重烧伤。

• 每年，近17.3万名孟加拉国儿童遭受中度或严重烧伤。

• 在孟加拉国、哥伦比亚、埃及和巴基斯坦，17%的烧伤儿童出现暂时性残疾，18%留有永久性残疾。

• 在尼泊尔农村，烧伤是第二大常见伤害原因，占残疾总数的5%。

• 2008年，美国发生了41万多例烧伤，约4万人需要住院治疗。

sections.heading: 经济影响
sections.text:
烧伤带来的直接医疗成本千差万别，但通常都十分昂贵。2014年的一项系统综述发现，每位烧伤患者的平均总医疗费用为88 218美元（范围：704美元至717 306美元）。

据估计，南非每年要为由煤油烹调炉灶引起的烧伤事故支付2600万美元的医疗费用。工资损失、对残疾和心理创伤的长期护理以及投入的家庭资源等间接损失也会加剧社会和经济影响。

sections.heading: 谁面临风险？ / 性别
sections.text:
最新数据显示，女性死于烧伤的比率略高于男性。而通常伤害情况并非如此，从各种伤害类型来看，男性受伤率一般会高于女性。

由于明火烹饪或本身存在安全隐患（可能引燃宽松衣物）的烹调炉灶，女性面临较高风险。用明火加热和照明也会构成风险。此外，自残或人际暴力也是危险因素，但目前缺乏对这些因素的研究。

sections.heading: 年龄
sections.text: 除成年女性外，儿童也特别容易受到烧伤影响。烧伤是非致命儿童伤害中第五大常见原因。尽管成年人监护不当是一大风险，但相当多的儿童烧伤是儿童遭到虐待的结果。

sections.heading: 区域因素
sections.text:
不同区域的烧伤率存在重大差异。

• 世卫组织非洲区域五岁以下儿童烧伤死亡率是全世界五岁以下儿童烧伤死亡率的两倍以上。

• 在世卫组织东地中海区域的低收入和中等收入国家，五岁以下男孩死于烧伤的几率是生活在世卫组织欧洲区域男孩的两倍。

• 世卫组织西太平洋区域需要医治的烧伤率比世卫组织美洲区域高出近20倍。

sections.heading: 社会经济因素
sections.text: 生活在低收入和中等收入国家的人遭受烧伤的风险大于高收入国家的居民。在所有国家中，烧伤风险与社会经济状况相关。

sections.heading: 其它风险因素
sections.text:
烧伤的其它风险因素还包括：

• 易受火焰灼伤的职业；

• 贫困、过度拥挤和缺乏适当安全措施；

• 安排少女做家务，如烹调或照料幼童；

• 基础病症，例如癫痫、周围神经病变、生理残疾和智障等；

• 酗酒和吸烟；

• 容易接触到可以伤人的化学品（例如用硫酸浇泼他人）；

• 用煤油作为非电动家用器具的燃料；以及

• 液化气和电器安全措施不足。

sections.heading: 哪些情况下会发生烧伤？
sections.text: 烧伤主要发生在家庭和工作场所。孟加拉国和埃塞俄比亚开展的社区调查结果显示，80-90%的烧伤发生在家中。儿童和妇女往往在家庭厨房中被烧伤，包括打翻装有高温液体或有火焰的容器，或烹调炉灶爆炸。男性通常在工作场所被火焰烧伤、被烫伤或被化学品和电灼伤。

sections.heading: 预防
sections.text:
烧伤可以预防。通过将预防策略与改善烧伤患者医疗相结合，高收入国家在降低烧伤死亡率方面取得了很大进展。大多数预防和医疗进展未在低收入和中等收入国家中得到充分应用。如果在此方面作出进一步努力，可大幅降低烧伤死亡率和残疾率。

预防策略应强调各种烧伤的危害，教育高危人群，并开展社区急救培训。应跨部门开展有效的烧伤预防计划，并应作出广泛努力，以便：

• 提高认识；

• 制定并执行有效政策；

• 说明负担并确定风险因素；

• 制定研究重点，促进开发有前途的干预措施；

• 提供烧伤预防规划；

• 加强烧伤护理；

• 加强能力，以开展上述各项工作。

《 世卫组织烧伤预防与护理计划 》详细阐述了这七项工作。

此外，为降低烧伤风险，还对个人、社区和公共卫生官员提出了若干具体建议。

• 在家庭环境中，包围火焰并限制明火高度。

• 推广更安全的烹调炉灶和危险性较低的燃料，并开展有关宽松衣物容易着火的教育。

• 应用房屋设计和建材安全法规，并鼓励家庭检查。

• 改善烹调炉灶的设计，特别是增强稳定性和预防儿童接触。

• 降低热水龙头中的水温。

• 促进消防教育并在家中使用烟雾探测器、喷洒灭火器和火灾逃生系统。

• 推广并遵守工业安全法规，并在儿童睡衣中使用阻燃面料。

• 避免在床上吸烟，并鼓励使用加装儿童安全装置的打火机。

• 推动制定关于生产防火安全卷烟的法律。

• 改善癫痫治疗，特别是在发展中国家。

• 鼓励进一步发展烧伤护理系统，包括对卫生保健提供者进行适当分诊和烧伤患者管理方面的培训。

• 支持开发和推广明火或煤油炉烹调时使用的阻燃围裙。

sections.heading: 急救
sections.text: 烧伤急救的基本指南如下。

sections.heading: 应当做什么
sections.text:
• 通过移除衣物和向烧伤处浇水，终止烧伤过程。

• 患者在地面翻滚或用毯子包裹，或用水或其它灭火液体扑灭火焰。

• 使用清凉流水降低烧伤部位的温度。

• 发生化学品烧伤时，用大量的水冲洗，以便去除或稀释化学物质。

• 以干净的布或床单包裹患者，并将其送到最近的适当医疗机构就医。

sections.heading: 不应当做什么
sections.text:
• 在确保自身安全（关闭电流、处理化学品时戴手套等）之前，不要开始急救。

• 不要在烧伤处使用膏剂、油、姜黄素或原棉。

• 不要敷冰块，因为这会加剧伤害。

• 避免长时间在水中冷却，这可能会导致低温症。

• 在卫生人员以及其他人能够对其使用外敷抗生素之前，不要弄破水疱。

• 不要直接在伤口上敷贴任何材料，这可能会引起感染。

• 在患者接受适当医疗之前，避免敷用任何外用药物。

sections.heading: 世卫组织的应对
sections.text:
世卫组织正在推广已显示可成功减少烧伤的干预措施。

世卫组织还支持开发和使用全球烧伤登记册以收集全球烧伤数据，并加强全球和国家网络之间的合作，以增加有效的烧伤预防规划。

sections.heading: 参考文献
sections.text: 全球烧伤流行病学的最新趋势：系统综述。 烧伤。2017年3月；43(2): 249–257 。

sections.heading: Key facts
sections.text:
• There are around 300 000 annual drowning deaths worldwide.

• Drowning disproportionately impacts children and young people. Children aged under 5 years account for nearly a quarter of all drowning deaths.

• Drowning is the fourth leading cause of death for children aged 1–4 years and the third leading cause of death for children aged 5–14 years.

• Ninety-two percent of drowning deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries.

• Resolutions endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly and the World Health Assembly provide a roadmap for global drowning prevention efforts.

sections.heading: Overview
Risk factors / Age
sections.text:
Young children are at a particularly high risk of drowning due to an underdeveloped ability to assess risk, and a lack of swimming and water safety skills. The risk of drowning increases when children interact with water outside of active adult supervision.

Children and young adults aged 0–29 years account for over half (57%) of all drowning deaths. The highest drowning rates per population are among children aged 0–4 years. At the regional level, drowning rates among children 0-4 years are highest in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region at 16.8 deaths per 100 :000 population. In the WHO Western Pacific Region children aged 5–14 years die more frequently from drowning than any other cause.

sections.heading: Sex
sections.text: The drowning death rate among males is more than twice as high as females. Males are also more likely to be hospitalized than females for non-fatal drowning. Studies suggest that the higher drowning rates among males are due to increased exposure to water and riskier behaviour such as swimming alone, drinking alcohol before swimming alone and boating.

sections.heading: Poverty and inequality
sections.text: Drowning disproportionately affects poor and marginalized people. Whether it be through the use of ponds, rivers or lakes for bathing and washing clothing, or using open wells for collecting water, the pattern of daily exposure in low- and middle-income countries brings a higher risk of drowning.

sections.heading: Occupational exposure
sections.text: Individuals with occupations such as commercial or subsistence fishing face a substantially higher risk of drowning. The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization estimates that more than 32 000 fishers die while working every year. Climate change has aggravated the hazardous conditions under which most fishers work, as extreme weather and natural disasters become more prevalent and destructive.

sections.heading: Climate-related risks
sections.text:
Climate change is causing more extreme weather events, such as floods and heatwaves. Drowning accounts for 75% of deaths in flood disasters. Drowning risks due to floods are particularly high in low- and middle-income countries where early warning systems and flood mitigation infrastructure are underdeveloped.

Heatwaves increase the risk of drowning. As temperatures rise, more people seek water for heat relief and typically spend longer periods of time in and on the water.

sections.heading: Transport on water
sections.text: Travelling on water, particularly in dangerous weather conditions or without appropriate safety equipment, can increase drowning risk. In many low- and middle-income countries, water transport is significantly less regulated than in high-income countries. Daily commuting often takes place on overcrowded and unsafe vessels, operated by staff who have not been trained to recognize hazardous conditions or perform high-seas navigation.

sections.heading: Migration and seeking refuge
sections.text: Increasing numbers of people are being displaced or migrating due to conflict, political and or economic instability and climate change. Many people resort to irregular channels for migration that are extremely hazardous, including across large expanses of water in treacherous conditions, often using overcrowded, unsafe vessels that lack safety equipment or are operated by untrained personnel.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.text:
There are many actions to prevent drowning. Covering wells, using doorway barriers and playpens, fencing swimming pools and otherwise controlling access to water hazards greatly reduces water hazard exposure and risk.

Community-based, supervised childcare for pre-school children can reduce drowning risk and has other proven health benefits. Teaching school-age children basic swimming, water safety and safe rescue skills is another approach. But these efforts must be undertaken with an emphasis on safety, and an overall risk management that includes a safety-tested curricula, a safe training area, screening and student selection, and student-instructor ratios established for safety.

• Preventing drowning: Practical guidance for the provision of day-care, basic swimming and water safety skills, and safe rescue and resuscitation training (2022)

A WHO investment case modelling investment in drowning prevention between now and 2050 shows scaling up just two interventions to be cost-saving. Through investing in day-care programmes for pre-school children and teaching children basic swim skills, 774 000 fewer children would drown between now and 2050. Furthermore, another 178 000 children would avoid severe, life-limiting injuries due to non-fatal drowning over the same period. Scaling these two interventions is projected to result in savings of over US$ 400 billion – a return of 9 times the value of the cost of scaling up the interventions.

• Hidden depths: the global investment case for drowning prevention

Effective policies and legislation are also important for drowning prevention. Setting and enforcing safe boating, shipping and ferry regulations are vital to improving safety on the water and preventing drowning. Building resilience to flooding and managing flood risks through better disaster preparedness planning, land use planning, and early warning systems can prevent drowning during flood disasters.

Developing a national water safety strategy can provide strategic direction and a framework to guide multisectoral action and allow for monitoring and evaluation of efforts.

sections.heading: WHO response
sections.text:
The Global status report on drowning prevention shows that drowning deaths rates have dropped significantly in recent years, yet drowning remains an urgent and often overlooked global health issue. Governments must reinforce proven prevention measures and prioritize drowning prevention and its integration with other public health agendas.

In April 2021, the UN General Assembly adopted the first-ever Resolution on drowning prevention, which highlighted links to sustainable development, social equity, urban health, climate change, disaster risk reduction, and child health and well-being. The Resolution called on WHO to coordinate multisectoral drowning prevention efforts within the UN system and announced 25 July as World Drowning Prevention Day .

• UNGA Resolution for global drowning prevention

In May 2023, the Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly adopted a Resolution to accelerate further action through 2029. Through the Resolution, WHO committed to establishing a Global Alliance for Drowning Prevention with organizations of the UN system, international development partners and NGOs. Further, WHO will prepare a global status report on drowning prevention for release in 2024.

• WHA Resolution for accelerating action on global drowning prevention

At country level, WHO is working with Ministries of Health in several low- and middle-income countries, guiding the development of national drowning prevention strategies and supporting delivery of evidence-based drowning prevention interventions. In addition, WHO has also funded research in low-income countries exploring priority questions related to drowning prevention. At regional level, WHO organizes training programmes and convenes workshops to draw together representatives of governments, NGOs and UN agencies working on drowning prevention.

sections.heading: 重要事实
sections.text:
• 世界各地每年溺水死亡总数估计为30万例。

• 溺水对儿童和青年的影响尤为严重。5岁以下儿童占所有溺水死亡人数的近四分之一。

• 溺水是1-4岁儿童的第四大死因，是5-14岁儿童的第三大死因。

• 92%的溺水死亡发生在低收入和中等收入国家。

• 联合国大会和世界卫生大会批准的决议为全球预防溺水工作提供了路线图。

sections.heading: 概述
sections.text:
溺水是因淹没/浸入在液体中造成呼吸受阻的过程。其结果分为死亡、发病和安然无恙。

各经济体和地区均面临溺水总体负担，但需指出的是：

• 低收入和中等收入国家的溺水死亡率是高收入国家的三倍多；

• 世界上一半以上的溺水事件发生在世卫组织西太平洋区域和世卫组织东南亚区域。

自2000年以来，全球溺水死亡率下降了38%，从每10万人6.1例死亡下降到3.8例死亡。尽管取得了这些进展，但溺水死亡仍是一个公共卫生危机，而该危机是本可预防的。按过去二十年死亡率下降幅度推算，无法实现许多可持续发展目标。预防溺水有助于实现多项可持续发展目标。

sections.heading: 风险因素 / 年龄
sections.text:
由于缺乏评估风险的能力以及缺乏游泳和水上安全技能，幼儿溺水的风险特别高。儿童在无成人严密监督时玩水面临较高的溺水风险。

0-29岁的儿童和青年占所有溺水死亡人数的一半以上（57%）。0-4岁儿童的人均溺水率最高。在区域层面，世卫组织东地中海区域0-4岁儿童的溺水率最高，每10万名0-4岁儿童中有16.8 例死亡。在世卫组织西太平洋区域，5-14岁儿童溺水死亡率高于任何其它死因。

sections.heading: 性别
sections.text: 男性溺水死亡率是女性两倍多。与女性相比，较多男性因非致命性溺水而住院。研究表明，男性溺水率较高的原因是接触水的机会较多，其独自游泳、独自游泳前饮酒以及划船等行为的风险较大。

sections.heading: 贫穷和不平等
sections.text: 溺水对穷人和边缘化人群的影响尤为严重。低收入和中等收入国家的日常接触水模式（例如使用池塘、河流或湖泊洗澡和洗衣服，或从露天水井取水等）带来较高的溺水风险。

sections.heading: 职业接触
sections.text: 从事商业捕鱼或靠捕鱼维持生计的人面临较高的溺水风险。据联合国粮食及农业组织估计，每年有32000多名渔民在工作中死亡。随着极端天气和自然灾害变得更加普遍和更加严重，气候变化恶化了大多数渔民的危险工作环境。

sections.heading: 气候相关风险
sections.text:
气候变化导致更多的极端天气事件，例如水灾和热浪。洪灾死者中有75%是溺水死亡。在早期预警系统和防洪基础设施不发达的低收入和中等收入国家，洪水造成的溺水风险特别高。

热浪会加剧溺水风险。随着气温升高，越来越多的人寻求用冷水解热，他们往往会在水中和水上停留较长时间。

sections.heading: 水路旅行
sections.text: 在水上旅行，尤其是在危险天气条件下或在没有适当的安全设备情况下在水上旅行，会加剧溺水风险。许多低收入和中等收入国家水面交通监管明显低于高收入国家。一些人日常通勤和旅行常乘坐过于拥挤的不安全船舶，或船舶操作人员没有受过正规训练，不知如何识别危险情况或缺乏公海航行技能。

sections.heading: 移徙和寻求庇护
sections.text: 由于冲突、政治和/或经济不稳以及气候变化，越来越多的人流离失所或迁移他处。许多人通过极其危险的不规则渠道移徙，例如在危险条件下穿越大片水域，并且往往使用过度拥挤、不安全的船舶，这些船舶缺乏安全设备或由未经培训的人员操作。

sections.heading: 预防
sections.text:
预防溺水的措施很多。如果采取覆盖水井、使用入口屏障和围栏、给游泳池安装护栏等措施控制水危害的发生途径，即可大大降低与水危害的接触和风险。

以社区为基础，对学龄前儿童进行监督照护，可以减少溺水风险，并能带来其它已经证实的健康益处。还可向学龄儿童传授基本的游泳、水上安全和安全救援技能。但采取这些做法必须重视安全性，而且必须在整体的风险管理系统下进行。应采用经过安全性测试的课程、提供安全的培训区域、筛查和挑选学生以及为确保安全性而设置合适的学生-辅导员比例。

• 预防溺水：提供日托、基本游泳和水上安全技能以及安全救援和复苏培训的实用指南（2022年）（英文）

世卫组织的一份投资论证文件模拟了从现在到2050年对溺水预防工作的投资，表明仅扩大两项干预措施就可节省大量资金。通过投资于学龄前儿童的日托计划和教授儿童基本的游泳技能，从现在到2050年，溺水儿童人数将减少774000人。此外，同期另有178000名儿童将避免受到非致命性溺水造成的严重影响生活的伤害。推广这两项干预措施预计将节省4000多亿美元，这是推广干预措施资金成本的9倍。

• 隐藏的深层意义：全球投资于预防溺水的理由（英文）

有效的政策和法律规定对预防溺水也很重要。制定和执行安全驾船、航运和轮渡规定对于改善水上安全和预防溺水至关重要。通过更好的灾难防备规划、土地使用规划和早期预警系统建立抵御洪灾的能力并管理洪灾风险，可以预防在洪灾期间发生溺水。

制定国家水上安全战略，可以为指导多部门行动以及开展有关工作的监督和评价提供战略方向和框架。

sections.heading: 世卫组织的应对
sections.text:
全球预防溺水状况报告显示，近年来溺水死亡率显著下降，但溺水仍是一个紧迫且经常被忽视的全球健康问题。政府必须加强行之有效的预防措施，重视预防溺水工作并将预防溺水与其他公共卫生议程结合起来。

2021年4月，联合国大会通过了有史以来第一项关于预防溺水的决议，强调了与可持续发展、社会公平、城市健康、气候变化、减少灾害风险以及儿童健康和福祉的联系。该决议呼吁世卫组织在联合国系统内协调多部门预防溺水工作，并宣布7月25日为 世界预防溺水日 。

• 关于全球预防溺水的联合国大会决议（英文）

2023年5月，第七十六届世界卫生大会通过了一项决议，要求在2029年之前加快进一步行动。通过该决议，世卫组织承诺与联合国系统各组织、国际发展伙伴和非政府组织建立一个全球预防溺水联盟。此外，世卫组织将编写一份关于预防溺水的全球状况报告，于2024年发布。

• 世界卫生大会关于加快全球预防溺水行动的决议

在国家级，世卫组织正在与若干低收入和中等收入国家的卫生部合作，指导制定国家预防溺水战略，并支持提供循证溺水预防干预措施。此外，世卫组织还资助低收入国家开展研究，摸索预防溺水所涉的重要问题。在区域级，世卫组织为各国政府、非政府组织和联合国机构负责开展溺水预防工作的代表提供培训课程和举办讲习班。

sections.heading: Key facts
sections.text:
• Bites by animals carrying venoms, toxins and pathogens are a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide.

• Globally, up to 5 million people are bitten by snakes annually, with nearly 50% of them ending up with envenomation – mostly in Africa and South-East Asia – necessitating prompt medical intervention with appropriate antivenom.

• Dog bites account for tens of millions of injuries annually; the highest risk is among children.

• Rabies is a significant health concern following dog, cat, bat or monkey bites.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The health impacts of animal bites vary with the type and health of the animal species, the size and health of the bitten person, and accessibility to appropriate health care. Paediatric cases are of particular concern related to animal bite injuries, with over half of the victims being children.

While numerous animal species have the potential to bite humans, incidents involving domestic animals are significantly more prevalent than those involving wildlife, and subsequent infections from wounds can lead to severe illness or even death. In general, the key to better outcomes related to animal bites is timely presentation of the bitten person for appropriate medical attention and accurately identifying the animal attacked. Animals of common concern:

• snakes

• dogs

• other vertebrates: cats, monkeys, rodents, bats, and other wildlife

• invertebrates: insects, spiders, scorpions, jellyfish, sea urchins, and stingrays.

sections.heading: Snake bites / Scope of the problem
sections.text: Nearly 5 million people are bitten by snakes worldwide every year, with 94 000–125 000 deaths due to envenomation-related complications, and 400 000 ending up with disabilities.

sections.heading: Who is most at risk?
sections.text: Most of snake bites occur in Africa and South-East Asia, common among people living in rural, resource-poor settings, mainly agricultural workers, women, and children.

sections.heading: Treatment
Prevention of snake bites and their serious health consequences
sections.text:
Prevention of snake bites involves informing communities about snake bite risks and prevention techniques including wearing protective shoes/boots; keep storage areas clear of rodents; raise beds above floor level; and tucking mosquito nets securely under sleeping mats.

Healthcare providers should be educated on snake-bite management. Public health authorities and policymakers should ensure appropriate supplies of safe and effective antivenoms to communities.

sections.heading: Dog bites / Scope of the problem
sections.text:
There are no global estimates of dog bite incidence, however studies suggest that dog bites account for tens of millions of injuries annually. In the United States of America for example, approximately 4.5 million people are bitten by dogs every year. Low- and middle-income country data are more fragmented, however some studies reveal that dogs account for 76–94% of animal bite injuries.

Dog bite fatality rates are higher in low- and middle-income countries than in high-income countries because dog-mediated rabies viral infection, and there may be a lack of post-exposure treatment and appropriate access to health care. An estimated 59 000 people die annually from rabies, and bites from rabid dogs account for majority of these deaths. While rabies is vaccine preventable and post-exposure prophylaxis can be administered soon after exposure to save lives, once signs of rabies appear, there is no treatment and the consequences are fatal.

sections.heading: Who is most at risk?
sections.text:
Children are the largest percentage of people bitten by dogs, with the majority in their mid-to-late childhood. The risk of injury to the head and neck is greater in children than in adults, adding to increased severity, necessity for medical treatment and death rates.

In some countries, males have a higher frequency of dog bites than females. Dog bites account for over 50% of animal-related injuries in travellers. Provoked bites are often due to attempts to feed or handle animals, whereas unprovoked bites often are associated with infectious stages of rabies.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.text:
Treatment depends on the location of the bite, the overall health condition of the bitten person and whether the dog is vaccinated against rabies. It is recommended to confine the dog and observe daily for 10 days under the supervision of a veterinarian, and in coordination with local public health authorities. The main principles of care include:

• early medical management

• irrigation and cleansing of the wound with soap and running water for 15 minutes

• primary closure if the wound is low risk for developing infection

• prophylactic antibiotics for high-risk wounds or people with immune deficiency

• rabies post-exposure treatment depending on the dog vaccination status

• administration of tetanus vaccine if the person has not been adequately vaccinated.

sections.heading: Prevention of dog bites and their serious health consequences
sections.text:
Communities – especially children – should be educated about the risks of dog bites and prevention including avoiding stray dogs and never leaving a child unattended around any dog.

Health-care providers should be educated on the appropriate management of dog bites. Health authorities and policymakers should ensure rabies control within dog populations, ensure appropriate supplies of rabies vaccines and post exposure treatments for potential rabies exposure in people.

sections.heading: Other vertebrate bites: cats, monkeys, bats and rodents / Scope of the problem
sections.text:
Cat bites: Worldwide, cat bites account for 2–50% of injuries related to animal bites, second to dog bites. In Italy, the incidence of cat-related injuries is 18 per 100 000 population; while in the United States cat bites result in 66 000 emergency departments visits yearly. Cat bites are associated with rabies viral infections and several bacterial infections related to bartonella, brucella, leptospira, and campylobacter species. The likelihood of a cat bite becoming infected is double of that of a dog bite.

Monkey bites: Monkey bites account for 2–21% of animal bite injuries. Two studies from India reported monkey bites to be the second common source of bite injuries next to dogs bite injuries. Monkey bites are associated with rabies, simian retroviruses, herpes B virus, and mpox infections, as well as bacterial infections related to salmonella and campylobacter species.

Bat bites: Bats are a reservoir for rabies virus worldwide and their bites might not leave recognizable marks making it challenging to determine the risk of exposure. While there are no worldwide estimates on bat bites, bats are the leading cause of rabies deaths in the United States. In Latin America, the risk of bites from hematophagous bats poses the risk of rabies for humans.

Rodent and other wildlife bites: Rats, mice, squirrels, chipmunks and ferrets are commonly associated with bite injuries. Rabies is relatively rare in domestic rodents; however, the bite injuries may lead to bacterial infections of leptospira, salmonella species and hantavirus infections.

Bites by raccoons, skunks, and foxes are often associated with rabies exposure in the United States. While injuries to vital organs are to be cautious of, bites by birds are rarely associated with life-threatening infections.

sections.heading: Who is most at risk?
sections.text:
Cat bites: Female adults have the highest rate of cat bites. However, similar to dog bites, cat bites are particularly more serious in children with injuries to the face, neck and head.

Monkey bites: Monkey bites are an important risk among travellers, after dog bites. Occupational and recreational exposures to monkey bites are related to animal control, veterinary, zoologist, wildlife professions, and hunting or trapping animals.

Bat bites: People are often exposed to bat bites because of occupational or recreational activities that involve regular handling of bats such as animal control and wildlife workers, veterinary staff and zoologists. Travellers to rabies-enzootic areas are also at risk of exposure.

Rodent and other wildlife bites: Owning small rodents as pet animals often lead to bite incidents related to feeding and interacting.

Bite injuries by any wildlife to be considered as risky exposures.

sections.heading: Treatment
Prevention of animal bites and their serious health consequences
sections.text:
Communities and travellers in the rabies enzootic areas should be informed about the risks of animal bites and prevention techniques including vaccinating domestic cats against rabies, avoiding intentional contact with wildlife, and reaching out to animal control or a public health agency for assistance.

Health-care providers, health authorities and policymakers should ensure availability of rabies vaccines and controlling infection within animal populations.

sections.heading: Invertebrate stings and bites:  insects, spiders, scorpions, jellyfish, sea urchins and stingrays / Scope of the problem
sections.text:
Stinging or biting insects such as bees, wasps, fire ants, hornets; bites by venomous spiders; as well as scorpion bites can cause a spectrum of health effects ranging from mild discomfort or pain to a potentially lethal reaction in individuals allergic to their venom.

Bites by tropical marine invertebrates such as jellyfish, stingrays and sea urchins can cause mild to life threatening reactions due to envenomation.

sections.heading: Who is most at risk?
sections.text:
Individuals who are allergic to the insect venom or immunodeficient are at high risk.

Marine invertebrate exposures are related to recreational activities including beach walking, swimming and surfing.

sections.heading: Treatment
Prevention of invertebrate bites and their serious health consequences
sections.text:
Communities and travellers in the high-risk areas should be informed about the risks of these invertebrate bites and prevention techniques including avoiding intentional contact, wearing protective clothing during outdoor activities.

Health-care providers should be educated on the appropriate management of these injuries including the variations of clinical symptoms elicited in individuals with potential to develop allergic reactions to the envenomation.

sections.heading: WHO response
sections.text:
WHO is working to address the public health problem of animal bite injuries.

For snake bites: snakebite envenoming fact sheet

For rabies: rabies fact sheet

For all other animal-bite injuries, WHO prioritizes data collection initiatives to estimate the burden and risk factors; advocates the strengthening of emergency response; and promotes research initiatives that focus on effective prevention interventions and populations most affected.

sections.heading: 重要事实
sections.text:
• 在世界各地，人们被携带毒液、毒素和病原体的动物咬伤是一个重大的疾病和死亡因素。

• 在全球范围内，每年有多达500万人被蛇咬伤，其中近 50% 的人被毒蛇咬伤（主要在非洲和东南亚）。被毒蛇咬伤后，需要及时使用适当的抗蛇毒血清进行医疗救治。

• 狗咬每年导致数千万人受伤；儿童风险最高。

• 在被狗、猫、蝙蝠或猴子咬伤之后患狂犬病是一项重大健康问题。

sections.heading: 概述
sections.text:
动物咬伤的健康后果取决于该动物物种类型和健康状况、被咬伤者的个头和健康状况以及是否能够获得适当的医疗救治。一半以上受害者是儿童，因此，动物咬伤儿童病例尤其令人担忧。

许多种动物都有可能咬伤人类。被家畜咬伤的事件比被野生动物咬伤的事件更为普遍。随后伤口感染可能导致严重疾病甚至死亡。一般来说，被动物咬伤后，善后关键是及时将被咬伤者送医接受适当救治，并准确识别所涉动物。通常造成咬伤问题的动物有：

• 蛇

• 狗

• 其他脊椎动物：猫、猴、啮齿动物、蝙蝠、其他野生动物

• 无脊椎动物：昆虫、蜘蛛、蝎子、水母、海胆和黄貂鱼。

sections.heading: 蛇咬伤 / 问题的范围
sections.text: 全世界每年有近500万人 被蛇咬伤 ，其中9.4万-12.5万人死于毒液引起的并发症，40万人被蛇咬伤后留有残疾。

sections.heading: 什么人风险最大？
sections.text: 大多数蛇咬伤事件发生在非洲和东南亚，被咬伤者往往是生活在农村和贫困地区的农民、妇女和儿童。

sections.heading: 治疗
sections.text:
及时就医是关键。主要救治措施包括：

• 立即完全固定被咬的身体部位，并迅速送到最近的医疗机构就医；

• 清洁伤口以降低感染风险；

• 避免使用止血带，并避免切割伤口；

• 用针对当地蛇种的适当抗蛇毒血清进行治疗；

• 提供支持性治疗：通气支持；

• 如果被咬者此前没有适当接种破伤风疫苗，应为其接种破伤风疫苗。

sections.heading: 预防蛇咬伤及其严重健康后果
sections.text:
为预防蛇咬伤，应向社区宣讲蛇咬伤风险和预防手段，预防措施有：穿防护鞋或靴子；储藏区防啮齿动物；床铺高于地面；将蚊帐下沿严实地塞到床垫底下。

应向医务人员讲解蛇咬伤处理知识。公共卫生当局和政策制定者应确保向社区提供安全有效的抗蛇毒血清。

sections.heading: 狗咬伤 / 问题的范围
sections.text:
对于每年发生多少狗咬事件并无全球估计数字。但有研究表明，狗咬每年导致上千万人受伤。例如，在美国，每年约有450万人被狗咬伤。低收入和中等收入国家的数据更为欠缺，但有一些研究表明，动物咬伤事件中有76%-94%是狗造成的。

低收入和中等收入国家的狗咬伤死亡率高于高收入国家，因为这些国家存在由狗携带的 狂犬病 病毒感染问题，而且受害者被咬后往往得不到及时处理或医疗救治。据估计，每年有5.9万人死于狂犬病，其中绝大部分是由于被患有狂犬病的犬只咬伤。可以接种疫苗预防狂犬病，并且可在暴露后立即采取暴露后预防措施以挽救生命，但是，一旦出现狂犬病体征，即已无法治疗，患者最终会死亡。

sections.heading: 什么人风险最大？
sections.text:
狗咬伤最多的是儿童，特别是中大童。和成人相比，儿童头部和颈部被咬伤的风险较高，也就是说，儿童被咬伤的后果会更严重，更需要送医治疗，死亡率也更高。

在一些国家，男性被狗咬伤的频率高于女性。对旅行者而言，狗咬占所有动物伤害事件的半数以上。诱发性咬伤通常是因人试图喂养或处理动物所致，而无诱因咬伤通常与狂犬病感染期有关。

sections.heading: 治疗
sections.text:
治疗取决于咬伤部位、被咬者的整体健康状况以及咬人的狗是否接种过狂犬病疫苗。建议在兽医的监督下，并与当地公共卫生当局协调，将狗禁闭并观察 10 天。主要处理原则如下：

• 及早治疗；

• 用肥皂和自来水冲洗和清洁伤口15 分钟；

• 如果伤口发生感染的风险较低，应进行一期闭合；

• 针对高风险伤口或有免疫缺陷者预防性使用抗生素；

• 根据该狗疫苗接种情况进行狂犬病暴露后处置；

• 如果被咬者此前没有适当接种破伤风疫苗，应为其接种破伤风疫苗。

sections.heading: 预防狗咬伤及其严重健康后果
sections.text:
应使社区特别是儿童了解狗咬伤的风险和预防方法，如躲开流浪狗，以及不要让孩子在没有看护的情况下和任何狗待在一起。

应培训医务人员如何正确处理狗咬伤。卫生当局和决策者应确保针对犬类进行狂犬病控制，确保适当供应狂犬病疫苗，并针对可能暴露于狂犬病的人进行暴露后处置。

sections.heading: 被其他脊椎动物（猫、猴子、蝙蝠和啮齿动物）咬伤 / 问题的范围
sections.text:
猫咬伤 ：在世界范围内，猫咬伤占动物咬伤事件的 2%-50%，仅次于狗咬伤。在意大利，猫咬伤事件是每10万人18例；在美国，每年有6.6万人因被猫咬伤而去医院急诊救治。猫咬伤可能会引起狂犬病病毒感染以及与巴尔通体、布鲁氏菌、钩端螺旋体和弯曲杆菌属相关的几种细菌感染。被猫咬伤后感染的可能性是狗咬伤的两倍。

猴咬伤： 猴咬伤占动物咬伤的 2%-21%。在印度，有两项研究发现猴子是仅次于狗的第二常见咬伤人的动物。猴咬伤可能会引起狂犬病、猿猴逆转录病毒、乙型疱疹病毒和 猴痘 感染以及沙门氏菌和弯曲杆菌感染。

蝙蝠咬伤： 蝙蝠是全球狂犬病病毒的一个宿主，其叮咬可能不会留下可识别的痕迹，因此很难确定暴露风险。没有全球蝙蝠咬伤估计数据。蝙蝠是美国狂犬病死亡的首要原因。在拉丁美洲，被噬血蝙蝠咬伤的人可能会患狂犬病。

啮齿动物和其他野生动物咬伤： 大鼠、小鼠、松鼠、花栗鼠和雪貂常常咬伤人。在家养啮齿动物中，狂犬病较为罕见；但被家养啮齿动物咬伤可能会导致钩端螺旋体和沙门氏菌感染以及汉坦病毒感染。

在美国，被浣熊、臭鼬和狐狸咬伤通常是暴露于狂犬病的一个途径。鸟类咬伤很少会引起危及生命的感染，但应小心鸟类对人体重要器官的伤害。

sections.heading: 什么人风险最大？
sections.text:
猫咬伤： 成年女性被猫咬伤的几率最高。与狗咬伤类似，如果儿童被猫咬伤面部、颈部和头部，可能会造成较严重后果。

猴咬伤： 旅行者被猴咬伤是仅次于狗咬伤的一项重大风险。从事动物控制、兽医、动物学、野生动物专业以及狩猎或诱捕动物的人可能会在工作场所或娱乐场所被猴子咬伤。

蝙蝠咬伤： 动物控制和野生动物工作者、兽医人员和动物学家往往因常规从事处理蝙蝠的职业或娱乐活动而被蝙蝠咬伤。在狂犬病流行地区旅行者也面临暴露风险。

啮齿动物和其他野生动物咬伤：有小型啮齿宠物的人常常会在喂食和互动时被咬伤。

被任何野生动物咬伤均应被视为高风险暴露。

sections.heading: 治疗
sections.text:
治疗取决于动物种类、被咬伤的部位和严重程度、当地狂犬病流行情况以及咬伤人的动物的狂犬病疫苗接种状况。主要处理原则如下：

• 及早治疗；

• 用肥皂和自来水冲洗和清洁伤口15 分钟；

• 预防性使用抗生素以降低感染风险；

• 根据该动物的疫苗接种情况进行狂犬病暴露后处置；以及

• 如果被咬者此前没有适当接种破伤风疫苗，应为其接种破伤风疫苗。

sections.heading: 预防动物咬伤及其严重健康后果
sections.text:
应向狂犬病流行区的社区和旅行者通报动物咬伤风险和预防手段，例如为家猫接种狂犬病疫苗，避免有意接触野生动物，并与动物控制部门或公共卫生机构联络。

卫生保健服务提供者、卫生当局和政策制定者应确保狂犬病疫苗供应并控制动物种群内的感染。

sections.heading: 无脊椎动物（昆虫、蜘蛛、蝎子、水母、海胆和黄貂鱼）叮蜇或咬伤 / 问题的范围
sections.text:
昆虫（如蜜蜂、黄蜂、火蚁、大黄蜂）叮蜇或咬伤、毒蜘蛛咬伤、以及蝎子叮咬会对健康造成一系列影响，从引起轻微不适或疼痛，到对毒液过敏的人死亡。

水母、黄貂鱼和海胆等热带海洋无脊椎动物的叮咬会因毒液而引起轻度至危及生命的反应。

sections.heading: 什么人风险最大？
sections.text:
对虫毒过敏或有免疫缺陷的人是高风险人群。

人们在海滩散步、游泳和冲浪等娱乐活动时可能会暴露于海洋无脊椎动物。

sections.heading: 治疗
sections.text:
治疗取决于动物种类、咬伤部位、临床症状和被咬伤者的过敏反应。主要处理原则如下：

• 及早治疗；

• 蝎子咬伤：用肥皂和水清洗被咬伤处，并尽可能冷敷；

• 海洋无脊椎动物：用海水冲洗被咬伤处，并在可能的情况下将被咬伤部位浸泡在热水（45◦C）中20分钟以减轻疼痛；

• 监测被咬伤者，注意其呼吸困难和急性过敏反应的任何体征；

• 如果适用，应使用适当的抗毒血清进行治疗；以及

• 预防性使用抗生素以降低感染风险。

sections.heading: 预防无脊椎动物咬伤及其严重健康后果
sections.text:
应向高风险地区的社区和旅行者通报这些无脊椎动物叮咬的风险和预防手段，例如避免有意接触这些动物以及在户外活动时穿防护服装。

应培训医务人员如何适当处理这些损伤，包括适当处理可能对毒液有过敏反应的人造成的各种临床症状。

sections.heading: 世卫组织的应对
sections.text:
世卫组织正开展工作，应对动物咬伤带来的公共卫生问题。

蛇咬伤： 蛇咬中毒问题实况报道

狂犬病： 狂犬病实况报道

关于其他动物咬伤问题，世卫组织重视开展以下活动：收集数据，以估算有关负担和风险因素；促进加强紧急救治服务；推动开展研究活动，研究重点是有效的预防措施和最受影响的人群。
